Making sense of Trump's unscheduled sudden midair disassembly of the American empire (permalink)
For generations, the American empire was the most powerful force on earth, and so we tended to assume that it was the most durable force on earth – surely anything so powerful must also be eternal?

But power and durability aren't the same thing, as Le Guin reminded us with her oft-quoted maxim that "We live in capitalism, its power seems inescapable — but then, so did the divine right of kings":
https://www.ursulakleguin.com/nbf-medal

Monarchs may be powerful, but that power is derived from a manifestly incorrect belief in special blood, a belief that requires monarchs to inbreed. At best, this produces heads of state who can't stop bleeding and also can't tell you if their blood is blue or red; at worst, it yields heads of state who can't speak intelligibly, much less produce another generation of royals:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_II_of_Spain

Oligarchy also produces a sequence of progressively weirder and more terrible rulers who rely on a mix of lies, flattery, coercion and personal cult nonsense to hold their coalition together in the face of mounting evidence for the system's bankruptcy. Thus Reagan begat GW Bush, who begat Trump, whose potential successors are a kennel of the least-charismatic chud podcasters ever to curse an RSS feed.

Trump's second term has resulted in a rapid, unscheduled, mid-air disassembly of the American empire. As Baldur Bjarnason writes, under Trump, America "first turned on their trading partners, then their allies in Europe, and then they delivered one of this century’s biggest economic and energy crises to their allies in Asia":
https://www.baldurbjarnason.com/2026/the-old-world-of-tech-is-dying/

The line comes from an excellent post entitled "The old world of tech is dying and the new cannot be born," about the impact of Trump's de-Americanization of the world on the US tech industry, and thus the world's relationship to tech more broadly. As Bjarnason writes, Trump's tech giants dominate the world because America dominates the world. It's not because the world likes American tech. As Bjarnason writes:

They are, more often than not, about as popular and respected as tobacco or pharmaceutical companies – some of them and their products are polling in terms of public sentiment in ranges similar to child molesters or authoritarian immigration enforcement entities – and their CEOs are some of the more despised public figures in recent history.
这些极不受欢迎的科技巨头之所以能主导市场，是因为美国的贸易政策坚持要求如此。它们可以无视当地法律，因为若阻止其行为将引发贸易制裁。诚然，美国科技公司偶尔会在海外面临罚款，但这不过是“造成社会苦难的代价清单——选择适合你商业模式的即可”。美国的主要贸易伙伴并未真正试图遏制美国科技公司的不法行径。
如今这一切都可能改变，这要归功于特朗普那种无法自控、反复自毁（以及毁掉美国）的冲动。但正如比雅纳松所写，这一切并非始于特朗普。他既是结果也是原因，而特朗普现象最重要的根源，是美国向金融经济的转型——这一转变始于里根时代，但直到奥巴马时期才最终完成。正是奥巴马让那些摧毁世界经济却毫发无损的华尔街掠夺者逍遥法外，尽管他们曾夺走数百万美国人的家园：
https://web.archive.org/web/20170130083243/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2017/jan/16/how-barack-obama-paved-way-donald-trump-racism
金融经济会吸干整个经济体系的活力，使其竞争力下降。维持亿万富翁的超级游艇生活，是以牺牲“科研、教育、基础设施和医疗”为代价的。金融化程度高的国家，落后于那些以制造而非提取或融资为核心的经济体。
几代人的帝国掠夺与本土投资共同造就了美国作为世界最富国家的地位。这种财富缓冲了美国向寡头政治的过渡：一度，这个国家既能供养吸血的亿万富翁寄生虫，又能继续自我投资。但当你能让一个亿万富翁的财富翻倍，只需牺牲一两个小镇；而要让一个百亿富豪的财富翻倍，则需要摧毁整个地区。
随着美国通过自我掠夺走向衰落，中国——一种截然不同的专制体制——却在投资本土产能与本土消费。中国远非治理良好的国家：像任何专制政权一样，它完全受制于极度不靠谱的官员意志，由此催生房地产泡沫等生产危机（更不用说独生子女政策带来的人口危机），并导致从网络监控到新疆集中营等日益加剧的压迫。
比雅纳松写道，这种中美格局给欧盟带来“双重困境”。倒向美国已越来越站不住脚：欧盟的存在很大程度上是为了扶持其本土产业，但美国如今已不愿放任不管。正如比雅纳松所言，美国经济政策现在变成“无论我们的寡头本月想偷什么，他们就能得手”。
美国科技已深入渗透到各行各业，以至于任何工业领域的防御都会触及“技术霸权”——在这里，只有那些支持技术、被技术支持、并通过技术中介的思想，才具有社会与文化合法性。
这意味着，继续在美国体系内运作，就意味着将经济和政治控制权持续不断地让渡给美国——一个由疯王统治的衰败帝国。尽管如此，欧盟仍存在一种强烈的、残留的本能，即保护美国科技产业，这迫使欧洲权贵们绞尽脑汁，试图为欧盟的技术监管仅限于空洞的象征性姿态而辩护，同时不惜一切代价避免采取任何实质性行动：
https://cerre.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/CERRE_Horizontal-Interoperability-of-Social-Networking-Services.pdf
但美国科技行业恰恰依赖于其他形式的美国权力——而这些正是特朗普一心想要摧毁的东西。特朗普推动的去美元化正在让世界远离使用美国科技进行支付处理和联网。美国帝国塑造了美国科技行业的形态。正如 Bjarnason 所写：“如果没有美国政治帝国的支撑——如果 Airbnb 或 Uber 只是本地初创企业——世界上会有少得多的国家放松监管和消费者保护，以容纳它们的发展，并让它们取得如今的成就。”
特朗普并非第一位犯下战略失误的美国领导人（毕竟，自二战以来，美国输掉了每一场战争）。但特朗普的失误与众不同，因为他“故意发出信号，宣告美国帝国的终结”。霍尔木兹海峡事件和关税政策正驱使人们远离美元，所有人都清楚谁该为海湾地区无谓的死亡以及因石油配给制引发的全球困境负责。
这对软件行业来说是个坏消息——这个行业早已将其价值主张从“我们提供帮助你赚钱或省钱的工具”转变为利用政治影响力和美元霸权去攫取、控制并掠夺世界各大经济体的各个行业。这种策略只有在掌控全局时才有效。
DOGE 摧毁了全球南方的卫生系统，如今特朗普的贸易谈判代表却要求这些国家承诺不触碰美国科技，作为恢复他们失去的那点微薄援助的条件。这些国家正在拒绝这些要求：
https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/zambia-says-us-health-deal-must-be-uncoupled-minerals-access-2026-05-04/
换句话说，一切都悬而未决。后美国的互联网正在一个后美国的世界中诞生，其面貌远非我们所能预见。Bjarnason 引用葛兰西的话说：“旧秩序正在消亡，新秩序尚未成形。”
我对一个基于国际数字公共产品的世界抱有高度期待：即用自由开放的软件取代美国那种掠夺性、有缺陷的黑箱模式，取而代之的是透明、可审计、值得信赖且真正由使用者掌控的替代方案：
https://pluralistic.net/2026/04/16/pascals-wager/#doomer-challenge
但——正如 Bjarnason 所说——即使是自由/开源运动赖以建立可执行许可证的知识产权框架，本身也是正在崩塌的美国帝国的产物。如果随美国一同崩溃的还有全球版权体系，那么我们将不再受制于任何障碍，可以自由地逆向工程并改进身边的技术；但与此同时，我们也失去了维护那些确保软件保持开放性的自由软件许可证的能力：
https://pluralistic.net/2026/04/02/limited-monopoly/#petardism
整篇文章写得非常好，就像许多伟大的文章一样——它提出的问题比解答更多。文中还充满了令人印象深刻的警句，比如这一句：
LLM如何影响生产力和质量？（就像含铅汽油一样。对于拥有数十年专业知识的用户来说，个人确实可能从中获益，前提是没有其他人使用LLM。而当所有人都使用时，结果将是灾难性的。）
建议将其放在周末阅读清单的顶部。

blocks.text: Welcome to the reading list, a weekly roundup of news and links related to buildings, infrastructure and industrial technology. This week we look at Tokyo’s cheap housing and expensive land, the House response to the Senate housing bill, an IED near an Alabama dam, Fervo’s IPO, and more. Roughly 2/3rds of the reading list is paywalled, so for full access become a paid subscriber.
Housekeeping items:

No essay this week because of a respiratory illness that is carving through our household like Sherman through Georgia, but I’m working on a piece about the build to rent housing industry that should be out next week.
I gave a talk about why major building collapse is so uncommon at Antithesis’ Bug Bash a few weeks ago. You can watch the talk here.

The Economist on why the closure of the Strait of Hormuz doesn’t seem to have yet created a worldwide oil crisis: other exporters (like the US) have raised their output, and many larger importers (like China) are importing less. [The Economist]

On the other hand, it seems like supplies of various petroleum products are starting to get thin. The owner of an oil change company is claiming that US consumer motor oil supplies are going to start getting thin in a few weeks. [X] And European jet fuel stockpiles are apparently almost exhausted. [X]

Some Japanese snack manufacturers are changing to black and white packaging due to ink supply disruptions. [AP News] The disruptions are due to a shortage of naphtha, a light fraction of crude oil. Interrupted naphtha supplies are also apparently poised to cause disruptions to the Japanese semiconductor industry. [Threads]

The UAE has started to build large anti-drone cages around its infrastructure to protect it from Iranian drone attacks. [The War Zone] And it’s also building a second oil pipeline to increase how much oil it can export outside the Strait. [X]
Thanks to Trump’s Jones Act Waiver, there have now been at least 45 cargo trips between US ports via non-US ships. [Cato]

Alex Armlovich on how making it easier to build housing both reduces rents and increases land values in the city of Tokyo. “The famous (relative) cheapness of Tokyo housing is not a story about cheap land. A one-acre detached house in central Tokyo would cost more than $100 million in dirt before you broke ground. The land is pricey but the structures are cheap. Admittedly, Tokyo’s rents and prices are not as cheap per square foot as buildings in the US Sunbelt’s midsize cities, but cheap by the standards of any 10-million-plus Anglosphere metro area. Tokyo built its way to relative affordability without ending up with low land values, and the values themselves look reasonable for a productive, agglomerated megacity that simply didn’t artificially restrict its own supply.” [Abundance and Growth]

Ezra Klein moderates a debate on housing policy between the leading Democrat candidates for Governor. [YouTube] And CA Yimby declined to endorse any candidate for governor, not because none of them had good housing plans, but because all of them did. [Cal Matters]

The house comes out with its response to the Senate’s 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. The house bill notably does not contain the onerous restrictions on build-to-rent housing that the Senate bill does. [Politico]

Are homes sitting empty because it’s too expensive for people to sell them? “According to Flock Homes, for many retirees “the tax bill triggered by a sale far exceeds the cost of simply leaving the home empty.” This includes capital gains taxes (paid on the profit from the sale) and depreciation recapture taxes (which sellers of rental properties face). The federal capital gains exemption, which applies to the sale of primary residences, was not factored into the analysis of vacant homes. Mortgage payments were not included in the analysis, since many older homeowners own their homes outright.” [NYT]
Number of sellers vs number of buyers in the US housing market. [X]

例行事项：
本周无文章发布，因家中多人感染呼吸道疾病，情况严重，如同谢尔曼将军穿越佐治亚州般迅速蔓延。不过我正在撰写一篇关于“租建一体”（build-to-rent）住房行业的文章，预计下周发表。
几周前，我在 Antithesis 举办的 Bug Bash 活动上发表了一场演讲，探讨为何大型建筑倒塌事件极为罕见。演讲视频可在此观看。
《经济学人》分析指出，霍尔木兹海峡关闭尚未引发全球石油危机的原因在于：其他出口国（如美国）已增产，而许多主要进口国（如中国）则减少了进口量。[《经济学人》]
另一方面，各种石油产品的供应似乎开始紧张。一家换油公司的老板声称，美国的车用润滑油将在未来几周内出现供应短缺。[X] 同时，欧洲的航空燃油储备 reportedly 几乎耗尽。[X]
由于油墨供应中断，部分日本零食制造商正将包装改为黑白配色。[美联社新闻] 此次中断源于石脑油——原油轻质馏分——的短缺。据称，石脑油供应中断还可能影响日本半导体产业。[Threads]
阿联酋已开始在其关键基础设施周围建造大型反无人机笼网，以防范伊朗无人机袭击。[The War Zone] 同时，该国还在修建第二条输油管道，以提升通过霍尔木兹海峡以外的出口能力。[X]
得益于特朗普签署的琼斯法案豁免令，目前已有至少45次货轮航行于美国港口之间，且使用非美国籍船只运输。[Cato]

Alex Armlovich 指出，放宽住房建设限制既能降低租金，又能提升城市土地价值，这在东京尤为明显。“东京住房相对便宜的说法，并非源于土地廉价。在市中心拥有一英亩独栋住宅的土地成本就超过1亿美元。真正昂贵的是土地本身，而非建筑。诚然，按每平方英尺计算，东京的租金和房价不如美国阳光地带的中等城市划算，但在英语国家百万人口以上的大都市中仍属合理水平。东京并未人为压低地价，而是通过增加供给实现了相对可负担性，其土地价值对于一个高效集聚的超大城市而言也显得合情合理。”[Abundance and Growth]
Ezra Klein 主持了一场关于住房政策的辩论，参与者为民主党州长候选人的主要竞争者。[YouTube] 加州 YIMBY 组织则拒绝支持任何一位州长候选人，并非因为他们缺乏良好的住房政策，而是因为所有人都有不错的方案。[Cal Matters]
众议院针对参议院提出的《21世纪通往住房之路法案》（ROAD to Housing Act）发表了正式回应。值得注意的是，众议院版本并未包含参议院版本中那些对“租建一体”住房项目施加的严苛限制条款。[Politico]
房屋空置是因为人们卖房成本过高吗？“根据 Flock Homes 的数据，对许多退休人员而言，出售房产所引发的税务账单远超于简单空置房屋的成本。”这包括资本利得税（出售盈利部分需缴纳的税款）以及折旧回收税（出租物业卖家需承担的税款）。分析未将适用于主要住宅出售的联邦资本利得免税额纳入考量，也未计入抵押贷款还款，因为许多年长房主已全额拥有房产。[纽约时报]
美国住房市场中卖家数量与买家数量对比。[X]

blocks.text: Launching 2026

Android.
          Reimagined
          for the Desktop.

Aluminium OS is Google's ground-up Android desktop operating system — not a stretched phone interface, not a browser with apps bolted in. A real desktop OS, with Gemini AI at its core, launching across HP, Lenovo, Acer, ASUS and more in 2026.
Android Apps
AI Languages
OEM Partners
Free
OS License
The Foundation
Android grows up.Properly this time.
Aluminium OS — internally codenamed ALOS — is Google's entirely new Android-based operating system built specifically for laptops and desktop computers.

This is not ChromeOS with a Play Store tab. It is not an Android phone app scaling itself to a 15-inch display. Aluminium OS is built from the ground up on Android 17, with a completely custom window manager, a real taskbar, virtual desktops, and Gemini AI baked into every layer of the operating system.

For over a decade, Google ran two separate systems in parallel — ChromeOS for laptops, Android for phones — and it showed. Apps behaved differently across devices, engineering teams were split across two codebases, and Google fell visibly behind Apple's unified iPhone-iPad-Mac ecosystem. Aluminium OS is the decisive answer to all of that.

The name itself is deliberate. ChromeOS came from Chromium — a metallic element ending in "-ium." Aluminium follows the same pattern, but the British spelling highlights the prefix Al, standing for Android-Linux: an honest acknowledgment of what this platform is built on.
Explore Gemini AI Integration →
Why Google Had to Act
Fragmented Engineering
Two codebases split teams and slowed innovation on both platforms for years. One unified OS means one focused engineering roadmap.
Consumer Confusion
Android apps behaving inconsistently on Chromebooks eroded trust in both products simultaneously. Native support ends the confusion permanently.
ChromeOS Ceiling
ChromeOS captured K-12 education but never broke into mainstream consumer or enterprise markets at scale. Aluminium OS is built for all segments.
Apple Ecosystem Pressure
iPhone-iPad-Mac proved that unified platforms win decisively in the market. Aluminium OS gives Android the same end-to-end integration story.
The AI Inflection Point
Splitting AI development across two platforms prevented Google from fully leveraging Gemini. One OS lets Gemini become foundational infrastructure, not a feature add-on.
3 Million Apps, Day One

Every Play Store app from launch day — natively, with proper keyboard shortcuts, mouse support, multi-window resizing, and desktop-appropriate scaling. No compatibility layer. No compromises. The app problem that kills every new platform doesn't exist here.
Desktop-Class Multitasking

Multiple virtual desktops, Snap Layouts, Picture-in-Picture, Task View — purpose-built for real work. Not stretched from a phone interface. A genuine window management system for screens from 11 inches to 4K external monitors.
Seamless Phone Sync

Copy on phone, paste on laptop instantly. Answer calls and texts from your laptop screen via Phone Hub. Resume tasks exactly where you left off with App Continuity. The seamlessness that Apple users have long taken for granted — now for the 3+ billion Android users.
Material You — Adaptive UI

The entire interface dynamically adapts to your wallpaper's color palette — taskbar, system apps, notifications, settings. This is the OS structurally adapting to you, not a theme pack applied on top. Spring-based animations and accessibility-first design in every interaction.
Linux Built In — No Setup

A full Linux container environment is a core OS feature, not a beta toggle. Docker, Git, Node.js, Python, Rust, Go, Ruby — all ready out of the box. Sandboxed for security but with full GPU access for hardware-accelerated development workflows.
PWAs as Native Apps

Figma, Linear, Notion, VS Code for the Web — install directly from Chrome as standalone desktop apps with offline functionality, push notifications, and full hardware API access. No Android port required for most professional tools.
AI Core
Gemini AI isn'ta feature. It'sthe foundation.

Every other platform adds AI on top — a sidebar, a chatbot, a menu item. Aluminium OS is built with Gemini inside the operating system core. It runs on your device's Neural Processing Unit. Your documents never leave your hardware for core features.

This matters beyond the privacy angle. A lawyer summarising case files, a doctor reviewing patient notes, a government contractor drafting a report — these people cannot send documents to cloud AI services. On-device Gemini changes the equation for those use cases entirely. It also means everything works in airplane mode, in areas with poor connectivity, and responds instantly with no server round-trip.
Cross-App Context Awareness
Gemini understands your work across all open apps simultaneously — Chrome, Gmail, Slides, all at once.
Real-Time Summarisation
Long emails, PDFs, meeting recordings — instant context-aware summaries in any application, not just Google's own.
100+ Language Translation
System-wide real-time translation in every app. Read any foreign document inline without switching apps or pasting into Translate.
Intelligent Window Management
The OS learns your workflow patterns and proactively arranges windows, prepares files, and opens apps before you ask.
On-Device Code Assistance
Write, debug, explain, and refactor code directly in the terminal — no separate paid extension, no cloud subscription for basics.
Natural Language Automation
Describe any repetitive task in plain English and Gemini automates it permanently as a saved one-command workflow.
NPU
On-Device Neural Processing UnitZero cloud dependency for core AI

Aluminium OS (ALOS) is Google's new Android-based desktop operating system built from the ground up for laptops and computers. ChromeOS was built on the Chromium browser engine — Android apps ran in a limited compatibility container called ARC. It is designed to compete with Windows and macOS across all market segments, not just K-12 education. Think of it the way macOS relates to iOS: same foundational architecture, entirely different experience built for a different context.

Previous attempts ran Android inside ARC — an App Runtime for Chrome — which was a translation container on top of a Chromium OS foundation. Apps performed poorly, crashed frequently, had no keyboard or mouse awareness, and resized incorrectly. Aluminium OS has no container. The OS is Android. Apps are native. The window manager, multitasking, and AI integration are built into the platform core, not retrofitted. There is no translation layer to degrade performance.

Aluminium OS（ALOS）是 Google 基于 Android 打造的新一代桌面操作系统，专为笔记本电脑和计算机从零开始构建。ChromeOS 原本基于 Chromium 浏览器引擎开发——Android 应用运行在一个名为 ARC（App Runtime for Chrome）的有限兼容性容器中。而 Aluminium OS 是基于 Android 17 重构的全新桌面平台，拥有定制窗口管理器、真正的多任务处理能力、原生集成 Gemini AI 以及内置 Linux 环境。它旨在面向全市场段与 Windows 和 macOS 竞争，而不仅限于 K-12 教育领域。可以将其理解为 macOS 之于 iOS 的关系：相同的底层架构，但为不同使用场景打造的完全不一样的体验。
Google 确认将于 2026 年发布。公开测试版已于 2026 年第一季度开放，相关硬件在 CES 2026 上展出。稳定版 1.0 及首批来自 HP、联想、宏碁和华硕等品牌的零售设备预计将在 2026 年第二至第三季度上市。Aluminium OS 不会单独销售——它将预装于通过主流全球零售商和教育/企业级采购渠道发售的认证设备上。
此前尝试是在 ARC（Chrome 的应用运行环境）内运行 Android，本质上是在 Chromium OS 基础上叠加了一层翻译容器。应用性能差、频繁崩溃、无法识别键盘鼠标输入，且界面缩放异常。Aluminium OS 没有容器概念，它就是 Android 系统本身。应用是原生的，窗口管理、多任务和 AI 集成均深度嵌入平台核心，而非后期附加。不存在任何可能影响性能的翻译层。

配备至少第 12 代 Intel Alder Lake 处理器或 MediaTek Kompanio 520 芯片、8GB 内存和 128GB 存储空间的 Chromebook 是最有力的候选机型。Google 正针对这些芯片积极进行测试。此次升级将是自愿选择，不会强制迁移任何设备。老旧设备、接近自动更新到期期限的设备以及仅配备 4GB 内存的低端型号很可能不符合条件。官方资格清单将在正式版发布前公布。

对于绝大多数办公任务——电子邮件、文档、电子表格、视频会议、网页研究和演示文稿——答案是肯定的，完全可以胜任。Microsoft 365 网页版应用和 Microsoft Office Android 应用已覆盖标准办公流程。唯一的例外是那些仅限 Windows 使用的专业软件：完整的 Adobe Creative Cloud 桌面版、AutoCAD 以及没有网页版或 Android 替代方案的行业专用工具。如果你的工作严重依赖这些软件，那么除了 ALOS 设备外，你还需要一台运行 Windows 的设备来完成这些特定任务。

在配备专用神经处理单元（NPU）的高端设备上，Gemini 完全在本地运行。你的文档永远不会离开硬件，即可享受核心的 AI 功能。它提供跨应用上下文感知、实时摘要生成、支持超过 100 种语言的端到端系统级翻译、智能窗口管理，以及在终端中的人工智能代码辅助——全程无需联网。即使在飞行模式下也能正常工作。除了隐私优势之外的实际影响在于：律师、医生和政府工作人员等无法合法将文档上传至云端 AI 服务的用户，现在可以完全使用 Gemini。入门级设备则采用云端辅助的 Gemini，其表现与其他云 AI 服务无异。

官方分为三个层级：AL Entry 起售价 299–499 美元（面向教育用户和基本用途），AL Mass Premium 为 500–799 美元（主流消费者及中小企业），AL Premium 则为 800–1,500+ 美元（面向专业人士）。操作系统本身是免费的——硬件成本中不包含任何授权费用。这意味着在每个价格档位上，同等配置的硬件成本都低于 Windows 竞争对手，因为后者每台设备额外增加了 80–150 美元的操作系统许可费。

如果你需要在一到六个月内购买笔记本电脑，日常依赖仅限 Windows 的专业软件，或者是一名追求原生 DirectX 性能的硬核 PC 游戏玩家，现在就买 Windows 吧。如果你主要使用网页版和 Android 工具，希望整个操作系统都具备原生 AI 能力，能接受延迟六个月到一年，并且乐于成为早期采用者，那就等待 ALOS。一个重要细节是：通常最明智的选择是等待第二代硬件（ALOS 1.1 或更高版本），而非首发机型——几乎所有平台在发布初期都会经历显著优化与改进。

是的，完全可以。设置完成后，你可以完全离线工作，包括本地安装的 Android 应用、已保存供离线访问的 Google Workspace 文档、通过 NPU 运行的本地 Gemini AI（高端硬件下核心功能无需网络）、本地存储的媒体文件、完整的 Linux 终端环境，以及支持离线的 PWA 应用。同步云端文件、下载新应用和系统更新、浏览网页、收发邮件以及使用入门级设备上的云端依赖型 AI 功能则需要互联网连接。
桌面的未来
Aluminium OS 将于 2026 年发布。

blocks.text: By Susam Pal on 16 May 2026

Let me share a very silly story from roughly 18 years ago!  In 2008,
  I joined
  RSA, the
  network security company named after the initials of the inventors
  of the RSA algorithm, Rivest, Shamir and Adleman, who were also the
  founders of RSA, the company.

There was a bit of a nerd culture in the workplace where topics like
  prime numbers, combinatorics, probability theory, etc. were
  discussed fervently.  A prime-number employee number was considered
  a lucky charm.  I had a rather nice large five-digit prime number as
  my employee number, which I remember being quite pleased about.
  There were internal forums for almost all kinds of topics.  A few I
  remember fondly were a mathematics forum where colleagues would
  challenge each other with mathematical puzzles and a similar physics
  forum where, for some reason, crafting contrived paradoxes using
  special and general relativity and putting them up for debate was a
  common activity.  The participants would analyse each paradox to
  determine if it truly was one or if it could be resolved into
  something that was no longer a paradox.  In fact, my
  Langford Pairing (2011) post was
  the result of a question I had stumbled upon in the mathematics
  forum.

The human resources (HR) department used to organise afternoon games
  once every month where people would self-organise into teams and
  solve a small challenge.  There was a cash prize for the winning
  team each time.  The HR folks were very well aware of the nerd
  culture and the fascination with prime numbers, but they probably
  did not know enough about exactly what type of problems we were
  fascinated with.  So in one of the monthly game events, the HR team
  gave us this challenge.

Write as many prime numbers between 1 and 1000 as you can in 5
  minutes.

The 5-minute timer started immediately.  Really, that was the
  challenge.  We all looked at each other in surprise, wondering if
  that really was the problem.  The game was already on.  No
  constraints were set.  Were we allowed to look up a list on the web?
  Probably not, otherwise what would be the point of the game?

There were five or six teams with a total of about 30 or so
  participants.  We began working on the challenge.  The first thing I
  did was load up the list of all 168 prime numbers from 1 to 1000 on
  my mobile phone and begin copying them meticulously to our sheet of
  paper.

I would learn later that another team had followed the same approach
  too.  The person writing their list decided to omit a few numbers so
  that it did not look like they had copied the numbers verbatim from
  an external source.  I think they were being overcautious because
  there were no rules, and all is fair in love and listing prime
  numbers.

I completed writing our list with about half a minute to spare.  We
  turned in our sheets after the timer ran out.  The HR folks then
  evaluated the sheets.  The winner was announced.  Our team won with
  all 168 numbers written accurately.  We won the cash prize.  One of
  the HR folks asked me later what formula we had used to generate all
  the prime numbers so accurately.  I told them that we had used the
  ancient formula of looking up a list of prime numbers compiled by
  someone else and writing it down.  We spent the cash prize
  immediately and ordered pizza and soft drinks for everyone.

The monthly afternoon games were not usually this silly.  The other
  games were more interesting, more challenging and better designed.
  But I don't remember what those games were at all now.  It is only
  this silly game that remains etched in my memory.

translations: 2026年5月16日，Susam Pal
让我分享一个大约18年前非常愚蠢的故事！2008年，我加入了RSA公司——这是一家网络安全公司，名字取自其创始人、RSA算法发明者 Rivest、Shamir 和 Adleman 的姓氏首字母。

当时的工作环境里流行一种极客文化，同事们会热烈讨论质数、组合数学、概率论等话题。拥有质数编号的员工被认为会带来好运。我的员工编号是一个相当不错的五位质数，我一直为此感到高兴。公司内部几乎每个主题都有专属论坛。其中几个让我印象深刻的包括：一个数学论坛，同事们会在上面互相出题解答数学谜题；还有一个类似的物理论坛，不知何故，在那里用狭义与广义相对论构造人为悖论并展开辩论成了常见活动。参与者们会分析这些悖论，判断它们是否真的成立，还是说其实可以被化解为不再构成悖论的问题。事实上，我后来发表的《Langford Pairing》（2011）一文，正是源于我在数学论坛上偶然看到的一个问题。
人力资源部门每月都会组织一次下午茶游戏活动，大家自由组队，完成一个小挑战。每次获胜的队伍都能获得现金奖励。HR团队很清楚这种极客文化以及对质数的痴迷，但他们可能并不完全了解我们究竟对哪类问题感兴趣。所以在某次月度游戏活动中，他们给我们出了这样一个题目。
在5分钟内尽可能多地写出1到1000之间的所有质数。
计时器一启动就开始倒计时，这才是真正的挑战所在。我们都面面相觑，怀疑这到底是不是题目本身。游戏已经开始了。没有任何限制条件。我们是否被允许上网查找质数列表？大概不行吧，否则这场游戏还有什么意义呢？
总共有五六个小组，加起来约有三十名参与者。我们开始着手解决这个挑战。我的第一反应是迅速在手机上调出1到1000之间全部168个质数的清单，然后一丝不苟地把它们抄写到我们的纸张上。
后来我才知道，另一支队伍也采取了同样的策略。不过，负责列名单的那位成员决定略去一些数字，以免看起来像是直接从外部来源照搬过来的。我觉得他有点过于谨慎了，毕竟当时并没有明确规则，而在爱情和罗列质数这件事上，一切皆有可能。
我提前约半分钟完成了整份名单的誊写。当计时结束时，我们把答卷交给了HR。随后他们评阅了所有提交的内容，宣布了获胜者。最终，我们队以准确无误地写下全部168个质数而胜出，赢得了现金奖金。事后其中一位HR问我，你们究竟用了什么公式能如此精准地生成所有这些质数？我告诉他们，我们用的是古老的“查表法”——即参考别人整理好的质数列表，再一笔一画抄下来。拿到奖金后，我们立刻花掉了这笔钱，请大家吃披萨和软饮。
这些月度的午后游戏通常不会这么幼稚。其他游戏更有趣、更具挑战性，设计也更好。但如今我完全不记得那些游戏了，只记得这个愚蠢的游戏。
